correctness.rationale: For any fixed state, invertibility gives a 5k-periodic two-sided sequence. Summing five F3 differences forces each column to have 0 or 3 nonzero entries. A zero column propagates to the all-zero word. For a nonzero column, an exhaustive two-zero cyclic-step analysis proves source zeros must be separated and successor zeros adjacent, an impossibility on a cycle; cyclic wrap rotations preserve adjacency. Every boundary k>=2 and the zero state are covered; a separate exact-integer program enumerates all 10 masks and all states for k=2..10.

value.rationale: Finch identified a natural permutation with exponentially many 4k-periodic states but no general control of other period multipliers. This exact all-k theorem gives a sharp arithmetic period-spectrum exclusion at the first larger multiplier 5, separating permitted 4k behavior from impossible 5k behavior. The two-zero mask lemma is a reusable structural obstruction and the invariant is the complete fixed-state count, not an arbitrary test instance. It is a natural infinite classification independent of numerical experiment.
